tasks.title: Section A: Landslides
tasks.statement: Resource Booklet Figure A1 represents a diagram of anticlines and synclines. Resource Booklet Figure A2 shows the remnants of a landslide that took place in La Conchita, California, USA (January 2005). Ten people were killed.

parts.question: Name two natural forces that can trigger landslides.
parts.reference: Suggested answers (award two of the answers listed): Precipitation (rainfall and snowmelt), Flooding gravity, Weathering along rock face fissures, Changes in water level, Stream erosion, Changes in ground water, Waves, Earthquakes, Volcanic activity. Award 0.5 mark for each correct answer. Award a maximum of 2 listed answers. Accept any other relevant and complete answer.

parts.question: Identify and explain two specific human activities that may contribute to landslides.
parts.reference: Suggested answers must have an explanation on how the activity contributes to landslides: Building roads or structures on steep slopes; Deforestation or removal of ground cover vegetation; Digging/undercutting at the bottom of slopes; Disturbing old landslides; Poorly planned alteration of drainage patterns; Nuclear explosions. Award a maximum of two activities. Award 1 mark for each identified and explained human activity. Award 0.5 mark for each identified human activity without an explanation. Accept any other relevant and complete answer.

parts.question: Specify the location on the diagram most susceptible to landslide activity (A, B, C or D).
parts.reference: Suggested Answer: D. Award 0.5 mark for identifying this location.

parts.question: Explain the reason for the location selected above (in 3a).
parts.reference: Suggested answer: Location D has the steepest slope exposed to rainfall run-off, gravity, bedding plain fracturing. Award 1 mark for a complete answer that contains at least the suggested elements. Award 0.5 mark for a partial answer. Accept any other relevant and complete answer.

parts.question: Clearly label the parts of a landslide on Figure A2 below, using the following letters as labels: A: head, B: foot, C: surface of rupture, D: scarp surface.
parts.reference: Note that D (scarp) could have two areas. Award a maximum of 2 marks for all parts of the landslide labelled correctly. Award 0.5 mark for each correctly labeled part of a landslide.

parts.question: Identify specific evidence from Figure A2 that indicates a previous landslide took place in the area.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: There is an old scarp visible in the top left of the photograph; Scree fans at the bottom of the banks (now covered by vegetation); Areas of slumping below the old scarp; Small landslide area below the slumping and above the road. Award 1 mark for each correctly identified feature that includes specific reference to the photograph. Award 0.5 mark for an answer that does not reference the photograph. Accept any other relevant and complete answer.

parts.question: Suggest two actions that can be taken to protect the neighbourhood from future landslides and evaluate the effectiveness of each measure that you provide.
parts.reference: Actions: Anchors and drainage prevention by planting trees/vegetation; Protection by building a containment channel or interceptor drains; Avoidance by selecting an alternative location for settlement; Protection by installing netting; Monitor the slope for signs of movement; Protection by building safety walls. Effectiveness of the Action: Student assessment of the effectiveness will vary; accept any relevant and correct answer that relates directly to the action they provided. Award a maximum of 2 marks for each identified and evaluated actions. Award 1 mark for identifying an action to protect the neighbourhood. Award 1 mark for a thorough explanation of the effectiveness of the action identified. Award a maximum of two actions.

parts.question: Name the season when post wildfire landslides are most likely to occur.
parts.reference: Suggested answer: late winter/early spring OR spring. Award 0.5 mark for correctly identifying the season.

parts.question: Explain why landslides are more likely to occur during the season you selected.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Freezing temperatures in the late winter can cause water in the soil to freeze and expand, increasing soil porosity. When the ice thaws, the water can easily infiltrate the loosened soil... Combination of snowmelt and rainfall in spring is likely to saturate soil... Reduced vegetation: less trees, ground cover vegetation and root systems... Wildfires damage the forest canopy... Award 2 marks for a complete answer that contains a reference to wildfires and seasonal precipitation. Award 1 mark for an answer that contains only one suggested element or listed reason without explanation. Accept any other relevant and correct answer.

tasks.title: Section B: Waves and coastline
tasks.statement: Resource Booklet Figure B1 shows a fictional coastline.

parts.question: Explain the energy relationship between wind and the formation of waves.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: The strength of the wind; The duration of the wind; The fetch; The depth. Award a maximum of 2 marks for two elements. Award 1 mark each fully outlined element. Award 0.5 mark for each partially outlined element. Accept any other relevant and complete answer.

parts.question: Describe four ways waves change as they move from deeper water towards the shore.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Wave shoaling; Wave breaking; Refraction of the wave; Wave diffraction; Wave reflection; Infragravity waves/edge waves. Award a maximum of four answers. Award a maximum 4 marks for four completely explained changes. Award 1 mark for each completely explained change. Award 0.5 mark for each partially explained change.

parts.question: Analyse Figure B1. Draw lines representing the path of the waves as they move towards the coast. Assume that the waves hit the coast from the north-east and have a wavelength of 14 m. Consider changes to the waves that may occur as they move towards the coast.
parts.reference: Suggested answer – the draw has to include at least four following elements: Wave lines remain parallel until the waves begin to "feel the bottom" at a depth of 1/2 their wavelength (7 metres); General bending perpendicular to coastline at depth < 7m; Bending towards headland and away from bay; Bending of waves into narrow bay; No lines or straight lines landwards of nearshore bar. Award a maximum of 2 marks for four correctly drawn elements. Award 0.5 mark for each correctly drawn element.

parts.question: Draw an arrow on the Figure B1 to identify the direction of the longshore current.
parts.reference: Answer: From west to east (from A to B). Award 1 mark for a correct answer. Do not award 0.5 mark.

parts.question: Justify the reason for the direction of the arrow you drew in 4a).
parts.reference: Answer: The answer has to include a geomorphological evidence (e.g. the river mouth and the sand build-up next to the pier) to justify their answer. Award 1 mark for a correct answer. Accept any other relevant and complete answer.

parts.question: Use your answers from the previous questions to develop a strategy for shoreline management in this area. Consider the way in which the various changes will affect the coastline and identify areas where you anticipate erosion and/or sedimentation in the future. You have unlimited resources, so you can build any type of coastal defence and change the land use patterns so long as your suggestions are realistic.
parts.reference: Suggested answer – part 1 (level marking): Students can take various approaches... economic, social and environmental aspects; groynes increase erosion downstream; dikes consider drift-related erosion; coastal infrastructure must be suitable for the site (50°N, winter ice); consultation with local people. Award 3 marks for a well elaborated answer, 2 for partially, 1 for poorly. Suggested answer – part 2 (point marking): identify at least two impacts of climate change in mid-latitudes (sea level rise, more frequent/intense storms, retreat of winter ice cover) leading to increased erosion. Award a maximum of 2 marks for both outlined elements.

tasks.title: Section C: Water stress
tasks.statement: Resource Booklet Figure C1 shows the current water stress by country – freshwater withdrawal as a proportion of available freshwater resources. Resource Booklet Figure C2 shows the projected water stress in 2050 (ratio of human water demand to water availability).

parts.question: For this question, refer to Resource Booklet: Figure C1. Describe the current spatial distribution of water scarcity in the world.
parts.reference: Suggested answer: MENA region (Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Kuwait, UAE); South Asia (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh); Central Asia (Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan); East Asia (Philippines, Indonesia); parts of USA, Mexico, South Africa, industrialised European countries (Spain, Italy, Poland). Award a total of 3 marks for at least three of the above regions. The regions must be ranked in order of water stress. Award 1 mark for each region in which certain countries and degree of water stress are mentioned. Award 0.5 for each region with specific countries or degree, or 1 mark total for three regions without mentioning countries and water stress.

parts.question: Identify and explain three main causes of high water stress.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Low annual precipitation combined with high evaporation rates; Excessive extraction of groundwater; Population growth; Agricultural demand; Industrialisation; Pollution; Inadequate water management; Transboundary water conflicts; Lack of infrastructure. Award a maximum of three causes. Award 3 marks for two identified and explained causes (Note: points per scheme indicate award structure). Award 1 mark for an identified and explained cause. Award 0.5 mark for identified cause without an explanation.

parts.question: Describe three socio-economic impacts of water scarcity.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Decline in agriculture; Food insecurity increases; Migration and displacement; Water conflicts; Health problems; Gender inequality; Industrial decline; Reduced energy production. Award a maximum of three impacts. Award 3 marks for two outlined impacts. Award 1 mark for an outlined impact. Award 0.5 mark for a listed impact without short explanation.

parts.question: Study Resource Booklet Figure C2. Explain why the countries of the northern Mediterranean are likely to experience major water stress in the future.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Climate change (summer drought, prolonged droughts); Growth of tourism (most visited, summer peak); Agricultural demand (intensive irrigation crops). A complete answer must refer to all three elements. Award a maximum of 3 marks for a complete answer consisting of all three elements (climate change and tourism mandatory, agriculture replaceable). Award 1 mark for each well explained element. Award 0.5 mark for each partially explained element.

parts.question: Outline three strategies for reducing water stress. The strategies must be related to actual, real-world situations.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Desalination; Reservoirs for freshwater storage; Reuse and recycling of water; Storage and utilisation of rainwater; Agricultural management; Public and domestic water efficiency; Restoration of ecosystems. Award a maximum of three strategies. Award 1 mark for each well elaborated strategy with an example. Award 0.5 mark for each partially elaborated strategy or a strategy without an example. Do not award listing strategies without elaboration.

tasks.title: Section D: Global energy consumption
tasks.statement: Resource Booklet Figure D1 shows the structure of world energy consumption by source from 1965 to 2018. Resource Booklet Figure D2 represents world coal consumption in selected countries and regions from 1978 to 2020. Resource Booklet Figure D3 shows the electricity consumption in selected countries and regions in 1990, 2000, 2015 and 2025. Resource Booklet Figure D4 gives the projected global primary energy consumption by region until 2050, made in 2010.

parts.question: Explain the difference between renewable and sustainable energy sources. Use specific examples of energy sources in your explanation.
parts.reference: Answer: Renewable energy is usable energy derived from a naturally occurring source or process that can be replenished faster than consumed (examples: solar, wind, hydropower...). Sustainable energy is a renewable energy source that can be consistently used without jeopardizing its availability for future generations. Not all renewables represent sustainable energy (e.g. hydropower, biofuel). Award a maximum of 2 mark for both explanations with concrete examples. Award 1 mark for an explanation of renewable energy and at least two concrete examples. Award 1 mark for an explanation of sustainable energy and explanation of one non-sustainable renewable source. Award 0.5 mark for each incomplete explanation.

parts.question: For this question, refer to Resource Booklet: Figures D1. Describe the main trends in the global consumption of oil, coal and renewable energy from 1965 to 2018.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Oil continues being commonly used with dips during crises (1972, 1979, 2007); Coal grew between 2000 and 2014 due to population and industrialization in China/India, latest trend stabilized; Renewable resources are growing due to agreements on reducing fossil fuels (Paris Agreement). Award a maximum of 3 marks for an answer that contains all three sources of energy. Award 1 mark for a complete description of each source of energy. Award 0.5 mark for a partial description.

parts.question: Explain three environmental impacts of using coal as a source of energy.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Air pollution (SO2, NOx, PM, mercury); Greenhouse gas emissions (CO2); Acid rains; Water pollution (acid mine drainage, ash ponds); Land degradation (surface mining); Health impacts. Award a maximum of three impacts. Award 3 marks for two explained impacts. Award 1 mark for a completely explained reason. Award 0.5 mark for a listed reason without an explanation.

parts.question: For this question, refer to Resource Booklet: Figures D2 and D3. Suggest three reasons why energy consumption in developed countries has not increased significantly, or in some cases has even decreased, since the 1990s.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Advanced technologies that require less energy in industries; Households afford to invest in solar panels, energy saving facilities; Heavy energy and raw material consuming industries outsourced to less developed countries; Shift to tertiary economy and decrease in population growth. Award a maximum of three reasons. Award 3 marks for three suggested reasons. Award 1 mark for any of suggested answers.

parts.question: For this question, refer to Resource Booklet: Figure D4. Due to the current geopolitical situation, Western companies are relocating manufacturing industries from Asia back to their home country or a neighbouring region. Discuss four possible changes to global primary energy consumption as a result of these relocations.
parts.reference: Suggested answer: Redistribution of energy consumption; Decrease in Asia's energy consumption; Increase in OECD countries' energy consumption; Industrial energy usage rebalancing; Global emissions redistribution; Energy efficiency and cost impacts; Impact on future projections. Award a maximum of four arguments. Award 4 marks for three explained changes. Award 1 mark each well discussed change. Award 0.5 mark for each partially discussed change. Do not award any marks to listed changes without explanations.

tasks.title: Section E: The Darién Gap
tasks.statement: Resource Booklet Figure E1 shows main routes of irregular migration in the world. Resource Booklet Text Box E1 provides basic information on the Darién Gap. Resource Booklet Figure E2 shows the location of the Darién Gap. Resource Booklet Figure E3 provides data on the annual migration through Darién Gap from 2010 to 2024 by country of origin.

parts.question: For this question, refer to Resource Booklet: Figure E1. Identify the primary direction of irregular migration routes worldwide.
parts.reference: Answer: From global South to global North. / From underdeveloped to developed. / Least developed countries to more developed countries. Award 1 mark for the current answer. Do not award 0.5 mark.

parts.question: For this question, refer to Resource Booklet: Text Box E1; Figures E2 and E3. Analyse the general trend and sources of migration through the Darién Gap. Justify your response with specific data.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Migration increased since 2010, intense growth since 2021 (>130,000); Highest peak in 2023 (>500,000), 2024 slightly lower (300,000); Cuba majority until 2015, Haiti 2016-2020 (100,000 / 80% in 2020); Strong increase since 2021 corresponds with Venezuela (150,000 – 300,000 annually); Crossings from other South American countries and overseas (China) since 2021. Award a maximum of 4 marks for a complete answer containing at least four required elements. Award 1 mark for each complete element, 0.5 for partial.

parts.question: Explain two socio-economic and one environmental reason for emigration from countries shown on the diagram. Use specific country examples to justify your answers.
parts.reference: Suggested socio-economic reasons: Economic crisis/collapse (Venezuela); Food and medicine shortages (Cuba, Venezuela); Political instability (Haiti); Authoritarian power/dictatorship (Cuba, Venezuela); Insecurity, crime and gang violence (Venezuela, Haiti); Extreme poverty (Haiti, Venezuela, Ecuador, Colombia). Suggested environmental reasons: Earthquakes (Haiti 2010); Hurricanes (Haiti); COVID-19; Diseases (cholera in Haiti); Climate change (droughts, floods in Colombia, Haiti...). Award a maximum of 2 marks for two socio-economic reasons and 1 mark for one environmental reason. Award 1 mark for each explained reason associated with a particular country. Award 0.5 mark for a general explanation.

parts.question: Suggest two reasons why migrants from countries outside South America choose the Darién Gap route to their destination instead of other alternatives.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Many migrants originally from Caribbean, Asia, Africa were already living/working in South America before moving north (COVID-19 loss of jobs); Strict border controls on air travel, USA-Mexico border and Caribbean coast make land migration the only option; Easier to get visa for South American countries and continue north as illegal migrants. Award a maximum of 2 marks for a complete answer containing both answers. Award 1 mark for each suggested and explained reason. Award 0.5 for suggested without explanation.

parts.question: For this question, refer to Resource Booklet: Text Box E1. Outline three threats that make crossing the Darién Gap extremely difficult for migrants.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: Heavy rainfall (landslides, flash floods); High temperatures and high humidity (dehydration, exhaustion); Dangerous terrain (steep, muddy mountains); Dangerous rivers (strong currents); Wildlife (poisonous snakes, jaguars, mosquitoes/malaria); Crime and violence (armed groups, drug traffickers, gangs); Lack of assistance; Navigation (getting lost). Award a maximum of 3 marks. Award 1 mark for each listed and outlined threat. Award 0.5 mark for a listed threat without an explanation.

parts.question: For this question, refer to Resource Booklet: Text Box E1. When Bajo Chiquito became the main reception centre for migrants, how might this have impacted services and built environments in the village? Give at least four specific examples.
parts.reference: Suggested answers: New catering facilities (rooms for rent, restaurants, food courts); New small grocery stores; Auxiliary services (currency exchange, mobile charging, wi-fi); Non-governmental/humanitarian organizations (Red Cross); Health facilities and mobile medical teams; Increase in built environment/transformation into urban centre with services; Congestion of town streets with people and tents. Award a maximum of 2 marks for a complete answer consisting of four listed elements. Award 0.5 mark for each listed answer.

tasks.title: Section F: Urban Heat Island
tasks.statement: Resource Booklet Figure F1 shows a satellite image of Birmingham and the surrounding urban area.

parts.question: Draw an isopleth (air temperature) map for Birmingham and the surrounding urban area. Draw isopleths at 3.9, 4.2, 4.5, 4.8, 5.0, 5.2, 5.5, 5.7 and 6.0 °C. Colour the map and fill in the legend.
parts.reference: Point marking: 1m – correctly drawn contours/isolines at 3.9, 4.2, 4.5, 4.8, 5.0, 5.2, 5.5, 5.7 and 6.0°C; 2m – proper selection of colour ramp (palette): 2 different colours ("warm" for temperatures over average 5.2°C, "cool" for temperatures under average 5.2°C) correctly graduated (award only 1m if student selected only one colour palette and correctly graduated it); 0.5m – correctly filled legend.

parts.question: For this question, refer to Study Resource Booklet: Figure F1. Analyse the satellite image and the map you drew in Q1. Identify the area of Birmingham where urban heat island has formed and describe the land use in the area identified.
parts.reference: Point marking: Area: city centre / central part of the city (0.5m); Land use: densely built area (0.5m), with little green area (0.5m).

parts.question: Explain four environmental impacts of urban heat islands worldwide.
parts.reference: Point marking: Award 1m for each named and explained environmental impact. Award 0.5m for only named environmental impact but not well explained. Impacts include: 1. Air Quality and Greenhouse Gases (increased energy demand, fossil fuel combustion, trapped air pollutants, CO2 emissions); 2. Water Quality/Waterways pollution (thermal pollution, stormwater runoff raising stream/river temperatures); 3. Energy Use (increased AC demand, power grid pressure/blackouts); 4. Animals/Animal ecosystems (food/water availability changes, extended growing season affecting breeding, thermal pollution affecting aquatic life metabolism/reproduction).

parts.question: Name three strategies that cities can implement to mitigate the urban heat island effect and evaluate the effectiveness of the strategies you selected.
parts.reference: Level Marking: Level 3 (5-6m): thorough understanding, explains and evaluates 3 distinct strategies, balanced assessment (advantages/limitations), specific examples/case studies, excellent geographical terminology. Level 2 (3-4m): good understanding, describes 3 strategies, attempts evaluation (may lack depth), some examples. Level 1 (1-2m): basic knowledge, identifies 1-2 strategies, limited/no evaluation. Possible strategies: Green infrastructure (urban forests, green roofs), Cool pavements/reflective surfaces, Urban design and planning, Water features, Heat-resistant building materials, Urban ventilation corridors. Evaluation covers: Cost-effectiveness, implementation challenges, long-term sustainability, adaptability, co-benefits, public acceptance.
